newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Bridgestone j/v sees lower sales.
newsitem.headline: Bridgestone j/v sees lower sales.

text.p: The new Bridgestone TG Australia Pty Ltd (BSTG) joint venture would not achieve 1996 sales results in its first year of operations, chief executive Ian Whitrod said at the company's official launch on Monday.
However, Whitrod said the company would begin exporting substantially for the first time in July 1997, with a A$1 million order for air bag covers to the United States.

The joint venture was formed after Bridestone Australia solds its automotive components division into a joint venture company between itself and Japan's Toyoda Gosei Co, the largest manufacturer of automotive components in Japan.

Whitrod said the new company had targeted A$58 million in sales this calendar year, compared to A$62 million for the division in 1996, due to declining car production numbers in Australia and a cyclical reduction in sourced car parts.
Whitrod said the joint venture would give Bridgestone access to Toyoda's technical, marketing and management skills.

He said that as a result of the joint venture, Toyota Australia would localise sourcing of some parts which were previously imported, and the new company would aim to increase exports, although he did not wish to give a target figure.
